q: Can upgrading an old induction furnace qualify for green or energy efficiency finance?
title: Finance readiness for a furnace upgrade
short: Possibly, if the new furnace uses clearly less electricity per tonne and you can prove it. Lenders look for your current kWh per tonne, the supplier's guaranteed figure, expected savings and how you will measure them. Whether it counts as green is the lender's call.
audience: Foundries and steel melting units planning furnace replacement

ul: Twelve months of electricity bills and melt logs.
Current kWh per tonne of liquid metal.
New furnace specification and guaranteed consumption.
Expected kWh and CO2 saved per year at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh.

p: Meter readings and production after commissioning, compared with the baseline.
If output rises, report savings per tonne, not just total bills.

senseible: Senseible turns your bills into a dated, traceable emission record, the baseline a lender reads before it looks at a green project. Lenders decide; finance is never guaranteed.
